note: Scenario-agnostic. Lives outside scenario JSON. Spec v1.0 §6. Career district (char.ray, char.dana, five scenes, two props, three vignettes) added without forking: one registry, two districts.
modesNote: 'none' is an INTENTIONAL blank: the node is a scene by presentation type but deliberately carries no artwork. It resolves to a null render block, the same shape 'messages' produces, and is set only through an explicit modeOverrides entry — never inferred from a missing visual block, which already means 'infer from location'. Added for the_instruction/escalate_bare, whose testPlaythrough declares the absence deliberate.

char.ray.name: Ray
char.ray.note: Ray Okonjo, manager. figure_c reuses figure_a's geometry contract only — basePoint, headSocket, neckSpan. Face, hair, proportion and wardrobe are drawn fresh. No rear figure: nothing in The Instruction frames over a shoulder and the player is never drawn.

char.dana.name: Dana
char.dana.note: Dana Whitfield, engagement lead. figure_d reuses figure_b's geometry contract only. Two registers because she appears in two nodes and one of them is an alternative to the other; a third would be an orphan under validator rule 8.

char.bola.name: Bola
char.bola.note: Mum. figure_e reuses figure_a's geometry contract only - basePoint, headSocket, neckSpan. Face, hair, proportion and wardrobe drawn fresh. No rear: no authored node frames over her shoulder. Four registers carry eight authored moods.

char.jay.name: Jay
char.jay.note: Oldest friend. figure_f reuses figure_b's geometry contract. The only rear figure in the district: he walks ahead in s1d1_jay_asked and s1d1_jay_quiet, which are alternatives to each other rather than consecutive, so both resolving to the same rear frame is correct - a player sees one or the other, never both.

char.tunde.name: Tunde
char.tunde.note: The legitimate route. figure_g on figure_a's contract, second body on it after figure_e. A working athlete, not a model. figure_g_rear deferred (D4): no authored node requires the framing.

char.dee.name: Dee
char.dee.note: figure_h on figure_a's contract. Nothing menacing in the build - if he reads as a threat the scenario collapses on Day 3. `exposed` is the cousin ask, the only time he is not comfortable.

char.kai.name: Kai
char.kai.note: Friction. figure_i on figure_b's contract. ONE register: both his on-frame nodes declare mood 'performing' and nothing else. A second would be an orphan under validator rule 8, and inventing a mood to feed it would assert what the prose has not established.

char.amara.name: Amara
char.amara.note: The outside read. figure_j on figure_b's contract. One on-frame node, s1d4_photos. Her other mood, 'flat', is on a messages node and draws nothing.

defaultWardrobeNote: resolve.py hard-coded 'home_casual' as the wardrobe floor, which no Career character has. Reading it per character removes fifteen otherwise-identical nodeOverrides. The two Neighbourhood entries restate the existing value, so The Secret's render blocks are unchanged.

scene.block.note: 16 nodes - the district anchor. Absorbs the landing nodes (D2), the shops, the wall and the long walk home: one deck-access exterior, doors one side and the drop the other. The walkway parapet is the occluding surface at y=600 and doubles as the wall in s1d6_sat.

scene.home_kitchen.note: 8 nodes, highest interior traffic. Five evening, three morning.

scene.jay_frontroom.note: Day 4 only. Sofa back plus sideboard, both solid to the floor - legs are the 2B.6 P0.

scene.jay_kitchen.note: Two nodes whose branches differ in DRESSING as well as light: Friday's party against Sunday afternoon. The one scene where data-time carries more than atmosphere.

scene.bedroom.note: Both nodes empty-cast, so this is the only scene exempt from the y=600 occlusion rule - no figure, no hands.

scene.cage.note: Floodlit Tuesday, daylight trial Saturday. The mesh fence is transparent and does not occlude: use the kerb wall or kit bags.

scene.jay_hallway.note: The photographs. HIGHEST occlusion risk in the set - a hallway has no natural waist-height solid. Use a built-in; a console table is exactly what failed in The Secret.

scene.jay_balcony.note: The threshold. Concrete parapet, NOT railings - railings fail continuous occlusion by construction.

scene.corridor.note: College, Day 3. Lockers or a fixed bench, boxed to the floor.

scene.bus_stop.note: Day 2's decision. The shelter's lower panel is the occluder.

scenesNote: D1: resolve.py now reads nodeOverrides.<id>.time first and falls back to default_time, so a room at two hours is ONE token with two atmosphere branches. The Career pair desk_evening/desk_day predates that and can collapse on a later approved pass - not this one. Streets declares five dual-time scenes against a SPEC-13 budget of ten tokens.

vig.table_three.note: establish beat 3 — player POV, third glass in foreground (§11.2)

vig.call_without_you.note: ask2_refuse_response panel 1 — a Monday client call, seen from outside the room

vig.kitchen_pleasantry.note: ask2_refuse_response panel 2 — the break-out kitchen, two people, nobody asking what you're working on

vig.june_two_seats.note: ask2_refuse_response panel 3 — two seats taken on the June phase

vig.eighty_in_twenties.note: s1d5_stall panel 3 - the only counted money in the scenario. A prose fact, not a state read, but the panel to check against scoring_keys_forbidden.

propsNote: Two new props for the whole Career scenario. The prose places only two objects in a room and moves them between scenes; everything else the district needs is environment furniture, which the scene owns.
scoring_keys_forbiddenNote: Union across all three districts. The Streets contributes 33 state keys, 12 derived bands, 3 dimensions and the outcome key. Without them negative_test.py passes against mapping.the_streets.json by having nothing to catch - a green firewall that is switched off. 'exposureBand', 'savvy', 'streetSmarts' and 'integrity' were already present from the other two districts; a denylist takes the collision harmlessly.
